newsitem.title: USA: Orphan says FDA clears Cystadane.
newsitem.headline: Orphan says FDA clears Cystadane.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration gave marketing approval to Cystadane, the first drug indicated for the treatment of patients with homocystinuria.
Homocystinuria is a rare, genetic disorder caused by various inborn errors of methionine metabolism that affects about 1,000 patients in the United States, Orphan said.
Cystadane was shown in studies to reduce elevated plasma homocysteine levels in nearly all patients.

Elevated plasma homocysteine levels are seen as the main cause of most, if not all, symptoms of homocystinuria, such as developmental and mental retardation; early thromboembolism; demyelinization disorders; skeletal abnormalities; osteoporosis; optic lens dislocation; seizure disorders; psychiatric disorders; and premature death, Orphan said.
"Reduction of elevated plasma homocysteine levels may result in the improvement of these clinical manifestations." the company said.
The most common side effects of Cystadane are nausea, gastrointestinal distress, and diarrhea, Orphan said.
Cystadane is available in the United States through distributor Chronimed Inc, Orphan said.

Orphan also said Orphan Australia received clearance from the Therapeutic Goods Administration, Australia's regulatory authority, to market Cystadane. Orphan Australia is an independent company with rights to market and distribute Cystadane in Australia and New Zealand.
